required_parts.name: stepped hull and prow
required_parts.evidence: Six lower, four deck and two spine segments (100 m wide, 36 m tall at amidships) with dark joints, a four-station prow wedge over a dark jaw with window bands, accent edges on alternate segments.

required_parts.name: surface detail
required_parts.evidence: About 350 greebles on the deck strips, flanks, belly, spine and stern; dark panel plates; flank belts with 30-window lines; two sponsons a side with turrets.

required_parts.name: turrets and tower
required_parts.evidence: Seven twin-barrel deck turrets plus four on sponsons; a two-tier conning tower with a windowed bridge, wings and a 56 m antenna forest of fourteen rods.

required_parts.name: engine pods
required_parts.evidence: Six layered pods aft (17 m outboard, 12.5 m inboard radius) with intakes, bands, shrouds, nozzles, glow discs, fins, pipes, stripes and window dashes, on dark pylons.

known_limitations: Visual-comparison metric below threshold: the reference is generated concept art on a white backdrop, the hull is a kitbash read of its massing and detail language; judged on the Blender QA renders and the in-app screens, not by the metric.

Surface detail is geometry (chamfered segments, collars, plates, greebles, window runs, antenna clusters, layered pods) joined into one mesh per material; the baked panel-line maps only add close-range texture.
Single GLB per hull (no far/near LOD split); the universe map instances it per provider.
